plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: Nodding, trumpet-shaped golden flowers rise from blue-green strap-like leaves. They carpet damp woodlands, meadows and old pastures in a golden haze, and the pale outer petals frame a deeper yellow trumpet.
plants.bloomingSeason: March to April, sometimes starting earlier in mild winters
plants.location: Woodlands, meadows and pastures of Britain and western Europe
plants.funFact: This is the native British daffodil, and it is smaller and more delicate than the garden hybrids bred from it. In the UK it is often called the Lent lily because it flowers around the season of Lent.

plants.name: Amaryllis belladonna
plants.description: Bare, sturdy stems shoot up before the leaves appear. Each carries a cluster of fragrant, trumpet-shaped pink blooms that glow against the dry late-summer landscape.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to early autumn, peaking around March in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Its leafless flower stalks inspired the nickname 'naked ladies'. Its common name, March lily, comes from its habit of blooming in the southern autumn, around March.

plants.name: Cyclamen persicum
plants.description: Swept-back petals in white to deep pink, with a magenta blotch at the base, hover above marbled silver-green leaves. They flower on rocky hillsides and in shrubland, brightening the cool, damp end of the Mediterranean winter.
plants.location: Rocky hillsides and woodland of the eastern Mediterranean, including Israel, Lebanon and Turkey
plants.funFact: After pollination, the flower stalk coils like a spring and pulls the developing seed capsule down toward the soil. This helps the seeds land in a sheltered spot.
